messages:
ava_sales: Hey team — live POC for Acme Corp. Customer says SSO stopped working after we uploaded their IdP metadata this morning. They can’t sign in, getting 500s on our side and SCIM provisioning shows 403s. Need triage.

sam_se: Thanks, Ava. Do we have the IdP metadata file they uploaded? Any error lines from our logs?

ava_sales: Uploaded metadata is here (customer sent): https://acme.example/metadata.xml. I pulled error from the POC logs: 
```
ERROR 2026-03-21T09:12:01Z saml: validateAssertion: signature verification failed: invalid_certificate
POST /scim/v2/Users 403  - token_scope_error
```

leo_infra: Signature verification failed usually means cert mismatch or metadata uses a cert chain we don't trust. Can someone paste the <KeyDescriptor> from their metadata?

maria_sso: Quick thought: Okta sometimes publishes a rotating cert URL instead of embedding. If they provided a metadata URL instead of the full file, we might have fetched an older cert. Also check the entityID in metadata vs what the SP (our config) expects.

jenna_poc: I have the metadata file that Acme uploaded originally, attaching snippet: 
```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://login.acme.example">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>MIID...</KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```

sam_se: EntityID looks like it doesn't exactly match the IdP issuer we had configured (we had https://acme-idp.example). That mismatch would make our SP reject assertions. Did we do a metadata import or manual field entry?

ava_sales: Sales portal import — I think the onboarding flow asked them for a metadata URL and we fetched it.

leo_infra: If the issuer doesn't match, our SAML library will drop it. Maria, can we log the incoming assertion issuer to confirm?

maria_sso: On it. Adding a quick debug flag to the SAML verifier. Also, the 403 scim token_scope_error suggests the SCIM token may not have groups provisioning scope. Two separate issues but both triggered by the IdP config change window.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: debug/saml-verbose -> staging at 09:40 UTC. No downtime expected.

sam_se: While we wait, ask Acme to check two things: 1) confirm the metadata entityID matches the IdP issuer in their Okta app settings, 2) confirm SCIM token scopes include provisioning and groups:write. Provide them our SCIM token format they should use.

ava_sales: Sent checklist to customer. They replied: they changed the primary domain from acme.example to login.acme.example last night and re-uploaded metadata but said portal import still shows older issuer.

leo_infra: That explains the cert/issuer mismatch. Possibly our metadata cache fetched earlier metadata and didn't refresh after their re-upload. We cache metadata for 10m. If they reuploaded during that window, we could have stale data. I'll force-refresh their metadata cache for the POC tenant.

maria_sso: Forced refresh done. Also pulled the raw SAML assertion from the failed login attempt — issuer is https://login.acme.example and NameID is email, but NameID format is unspecified. Our SP expects transient or emailAddress depending on tenant config. If NameID format mismatch, attribute mapping could break user provisioning.

jenna_poc: Acme says they use email NameID and want persistent login. They can switch format.

sam_se: Two paths: quick unblock = create a temporary hosted API key for the POC to bypass SSO for a few users (explicitly authorized), OR fix SSO mapping properly. Sales prefers SSO working for evaluation — but ok to provide temporary API keys if it buys time.

ava_sales: I'll approve temporary API keys for up to 5 seats for 48h if engineering needs time. Please add audit note.

leo_infra: Temporary API key created and sent to AvA via secure DM. Note: we should still resolve cert/issuer and SCIM.

maria_sso: After cache refresh I retried assertion verification — signature now verifies against the new cert. SCIM still 403. Looking at the request we see Authorization: Bearer <token> but token scopes = ["scim:read"], not write.

sam_se: Did Acme use the service account we generated or a different token? Sometimes Okta provisioning token needs explicit group provisioning scope when you generate the token in the integration console.

jenna_poc: Customer says they copied token from their admin to our portal. They will regenerate token with full provisioning scopes (Users and Groups) and paste back in.

maria_sso: Also noticed our SCIM client enforces TLS 1.2+ and requires SNI header for their multi-tenant endpoint. Their cert chain had a missing intermediate for login.acme.example — some SDKs tolerate it, ours rejects. Can ask them to fix chain or we can enable a temporary relaxed TLS mode for the POC (requires SRE approval).

leo_infra: I'm not comfortable loosening TLS without security approval. Better ask Acme to upload full chain to their CA or update their endpoint. Security is fine with temporary manual exception if customer signs a waiver, but that's SA-level.

ava_sales: I'll ask legal for a simple exception waiver. Meanwhile, can we test against a staging endpoint?

sam_se: We can simulate their token and cert locally — I'll spin up a quick mock IdP + SCIM stub and test mappings. If their regenerated token still 403s, we have reproduction.

deploy-bot: Job sam_se/mock-sso-run started.

sam_se: Repro'd SCIM 403 locally when token scopes missing. With correct scope token, provisioning works. Also reproduced SAML NameID format mismatch causing user entries to skip mapping (we log unmapped attributes).

maria_sso: Proposed fix steps: 1) Acme regenerates SCIM token with groups write scope; 2) Update metadata import to match entityID login.acme.example; 3) Ensure NameID format set to emailAddress in their Okta app; 4) Re-run SCIM reprovision (force sync) from our portal.

jenna_poc: Communicated steps to Acme. They completed token regen and uploaded full cert chain. They asked if we can re-trigger provisioning from our side.

leo_infra: Re-triggered manual SCIM sync for their tenant at 10:45 UTC. Logs: 
```
POST /scim/v2/Users 201 - created 3 users
POST /scim/v2/Groups 200 - updated 5 groups
```

ava_sales: Great — customer confirms users can now login via SSO and groups provisioned. They can proceed with the POC.

maria_sso: Leaving a note: we added an extra validation in metadata import UI to warn when entityID mismatch is detected and to prompt for force-refresh of metadata. Filed ENG-6421.

sam_se: Also added a small doc blurb for sales: "If SSO fails after metadata upload: check entityID, cert chain, NameID format, SCIM token scopes, and metadata cache refresh." Will share in sales onboarding playbook.

ava_sales: Thanks everyone. Closing loop with Acme and marking POC as unblocked. :tada:

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: debug/saml-verbose -> staging at 09:40 UTC. Logs archived to /deploys/2026-03-21/debug-saml-verbose
